editorial:
Imagine waking up to find your best friend has vanished without a trace. That is exactly what happens to Nobita when Doraemon has to return to the future. You get to see a much more emotional side of their bond as Nobita struggles to handle life without his robotic pal and those crazy gadgets. The vibe is a mix of sadness and hope, making you really feel how much these two rely on each other. It is a short film, but it hits hard because it focuses on the fear of losing someone you love.

What really works here is the pacing, as it moves quickly but gives you enough time to cry. The animation is classic and cozy, though some parts might feel a bit dated. If you are a fan of heartfelt stories, you will love this one. Since it is a shorter piece, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best colors. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this treasure forever.
endingExplained: Nobita spends the whole story trying to prove he can be independent so Doraemon will not worry about him. After a lot of hard work and tears, Doraemon finally returns from the future. He realizes that Nobita has grown up and can take care of himself. They have a big, emotional reunion, and the movie ends with them staying together, proving that their friendship is stronger than any time-travel rule.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves touching stories about friendship and childhood.
